title: JSONSchema
description: A top-level schema document that is the unit of identity and $ref resolution in the data model: it declares a dialect via $schema and a base URI via $id, and contains the root type constraint plus any named subschemas under definitions. Only the outermost schema of a file or registered document qualifies; nested subschemas do not. Use SchemaDefinition instead when the schema is a named, reusable subschema nested under a document's definitions keyword rather than the document itself. Use ObjectSchema instead when you are modelling the object-level constraints (properties, required, additionalProperties) of a schema rather than the document that carries $schema/$id. Use Reference instead when the element is only a $ref pointer to another schema, not a self-contained document with its own $id. Use SchemaComposition instead when the element combines subschemas with allOf/anyOf/oneOf/not rather than being an identified root document.

$schema.description: URI of the JSON Schema dialect/meta-schema the document conforms to (e.g. 'http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#'); set on every root document so validators apply Draft 7 semantics.

$id.description: Absolute URI that identifies the document and serves as the base URI for resolving relative $ref values (e.g. 'https://example.com/schemas/order.json'); set to a stable, unique URI per document.

title.description: Short human-readable name for the schema document, typically the domain entity it describes (e.g. 'Order'); set when the document needs a display label in tooling or generated docs.

definitions.description: Reusable subschemas keyed by name, referenced elsewhere in the schema via $ref: '#/definitions/{name}'

x-dr-standard: JSON Schema Draft 7 (draft-handrews-json-schema-01) §4.3.3 Root Schema and Subschemas, §7 The $schema Keyword, §8.2 The $id Keyword
x-dr-evidence: a *.schema.json or *.json file whose top-level object contains "$schema": "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#" and an "$id" URI
a schema registered with a validator by URI, e.g. ajv.addSchema(schema, 'https://example.com/order.json') or compile() called on a loaded file
a build step or decorator that emits a whole schema document per model, e.g. pydantic Model.model_json_schema() or zod-to-json-schema output written to a schemas/ directory
